body:
On the night of February 25, 2011, I went to go see Pendulum at the Wiltern. I went with a girl that I knew from school.
At around 8-9 pm, I consumed 5 30 mg Vyvanse via oral. I went into the concert. 1 hour later, I couldn't feel anything, so I decided to buy some E from a person I will refer as R. R sold me 1 Purple Paw Pokeball. Trusting that he didn't give me a bunk pill, I chewed it. 10 minutes later or so, I decided to smoke a cigarette. 20 or so minutes later, the nicotine (somehow) catalyzed the effects of the pill and I felt a roll about 25-30 minutes after I consumed it. (It normally takes about 45 minutes for it to kick in if I chew a pill.) Luckily, R sold me a very clean pill, with very good reviews on the internet. So, I go back to the girl I came with, and I dance with her throughout the concert. It's a typical roll: I felt happy, fuzzy and warm inside, and very social. That went on for about 3 or so hours. Once the concert ended, we went back into the car. (A person drove us from the city we were both from.) We ended making out inside the car, but she ended up passing out from extreme exhaustion. (She was completely sober.)
Suddenly, I felt a sharp pain in my chest. I checked my heart rate, and it was over 170 BPM. I had difficulty breathing, whenever I tried taking a deep breath, I felt an extremely sharp pain in my chest. One minute felt like an hour. When we arrived at my apartment, I was very jittery, still feeling the same effects an hour ago. Sharp pain and an extremely high heart rate.
When I went into my apartment, things started turning upside down. I collapsed on my bed, barely able to breathe. My girl was passed out on my bed. I stayed up all night, with the symptoms turning worse every second.
These sharp pains and the extremely high heart rate stayed with me for a few days. I felt like I was going to die until I came back to earth.
Overall, I learned my lesson to never mix ADHD medication (at least Vyvanse) with Ecstasy, because even to this day, I still feel subtle effects from it. (Difficulty being able to breathe.)
